subject: Re: Redwood deployment options & migration plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@lumen-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood deployment options & migration plan

Hi Alex 
2014 great chat earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Call recap:
- Use case: real-time summarization + customer support routing for Lumen's enterprise customers (PII + transactional data).
- Current setup: using VendorX hosted LLM API for embeddings and generation; some self-hosted GPU batch jobs for heavy nightly processing.
- Key drivers: latency (sub-150ms for edge calls), data residency and audit logs, predictable month-to-month cost as usage scales.

Deployment options we discussed:
1) Hosted API: fastest to go live, pay-as-you-go, limited isolation (suitable for non-sensitive workloads or early prod).
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation, better for steady traffic with strict SLAs.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation + KMS/HSM integration for regulated workloads 
2014 highest control, longer setup.

What we heard as your preference: leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of compliance and consistent throughput needs. You also mentioned a migration window in Q3 and a desire to avoid a multi-month architecture change during a product launch.

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll share a short migration checklist and sample pricing for Dedicated (attached).
- Could you confirm two things so we can tailor the recommendation:
  * expected RPS (peak and avg) and 95th percentile latency requirement
  * whether logs/audit need to be stored in your AWS account (S3) or in Redwood with export policies

If it helps, we can do a 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra lead and our solutions engineer to align on network/VPC and KMS details. Available times: Wed 10am or Thu 2pm PT.

Thanks ' I'll follow up with the pricing PDF and migration checklist now.

''
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing.pdf
Attachment: migration-checklist.xlsx

From: Alex Johnson <alex@lumen-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lumen-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood deployment options & migration plan

Thanks Marissa ' strong recap and thanks for the materials. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic profile: average ~12 RPS for generation endpoints, with spikes to ~60 RPS during business hours. Nightly batch jobs run on our GPU cluster for model fine-tuning / large-batch reranks.
2) Latency: target p95 <150ms for the customer-facing calls; for internal batch jobs latency is not a concern.
3) Data residency: all customer PII must stay in our AWS account. We need audit logs and request traces delivered to our S3 bucket and retention policy for 13 months.

Given that, Dedicated makes sense if Redwood can: (a) provide a clear path for KMS integration and (b) guarantee export of audit logs to our S3. Private VPC/on-prem is also an option but we prefer to avoid the full on-prem lift if Dedicated meets the controls.

We're targeting a migration kickoff in mid-August to avoid the July product launch. Procurement is cc'd for contract/timing questions.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, Lumen Analytics

- Audit logs: we can push request-level logs and structured event exports to your S3 bucket; retention policy is configurable from the Console or via API.

Proposed immediate next steps:

If Wed 10am PT works, Rishi ' can you take the deep-dive with Alex and bring a network/VPC checklist? Monica ' please prepare a skeleton SOW we can share with Procurement after the call.
